facts.text: The leopard cat is Taiwan's only surviving native wild cat species.
Fewer than 500 leopard cats are estimated to survive in the wild in Taiwan, mainly in Miaoli, Taichung and Nantou.
Being hit by vehicles is one of the main threats to Taiwan's leopard cats; some reports call road traffic the greatest threat.
Many leopard cats have been killed by vehicles on County Road No. 140 in Miaoli.
In Tongsiao, Miaoli, part of a freeway bridge was turned into a wildlife corridor with soil, rocks and native plants.
Infrared cameras recorded leopard cats, Formosan hares, masked palm civets and ferret-badgers using the corridor.
On Provincial Highway 3, thermal cameras detect leopard cats and display a warning on a sign about 1 km ahead.
Stray dogs and the misuse of pesticides and rat poison also threaten leopard cats.
Leopard cats sometimes raid chicken coops; higher walls or fences keep them out, but many small farmers cannot afford them.
